claim: Let \(k\) be an uncountable algebraically closed field of characteristic \(0\), let \(W_{\ge -1}=k[t]\partial\), and let \(B_1\subseteq T_1=A_1\otimes k[v]\) be the image of the first orbit homomorphism \(\Psi_1\) of Pham. Put \(w=v(v-1)\) and \(z=wv\). Then the ordinary center is exactly \(Z(B_1)=k+w k[v]=k[w,z]\), with presentation \(Z(B_1)\cong k[W,Z]/(Z^2-WZ-W^3)\). Hence \(\operatorname{Spec} Z(B_1)\) is a rational affine nodal curve, its normalization is \(\mathbb A^1_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[v]\), and the normalization map identifies precisely the two points \(v=0\) and \(v=1\) over the node.
integrity: The proof is symbolic and uses only the published orbit-map realization, the published localization and kernel statements for B_1, and elementary Weyl/commutative algebra. No computation is extrapolated to an infinite theorem.
scientific_limitations: Uncountable algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields, exactly the first orbit image B_1. No claim is made for higher orbit images or for positive characteristic.
title: The first Witt orbit image has a nodal ordinary center
